back: Software stored permanently in ROM or flash memory that controls hardware at a basic level, e.g. the bootloader.
Firmware that runs at switch-on, checks the hardware and loads the operating system from storage into RAM.

front: Layers needed to run an application
back: Applications run on the OS → the OS is loaded and run by the firmware (bootloader) → the firmware runs on the hardware.
A signal from hardware or software to the processor that an event needs attention.
A short program (part of the OS or a driver) that deals with one particular type of interrupt.
Key pressed, mouse moved or clicked, printer out of paper or buffer empty, disk transfer finished.
Division by zero; two processes trying to access the same memory location; a program requesting an OS service.
Checked at end of FDE cycle → priority compared → registers saved → ISR run → registers restored → task resumes.
